messages:
Maya (Payments): Heads up — QuickPay reported an ACH debit that was returned this morning. payout_id p-8f3a2, amount $12,450. Bank returned it as 'invalid routing number' but the payload we sent included both routing and account. Can someone look?

Brian (Support): Thanks, Maya. Ticket #QKP-4521. Customer pasted bank message: 'Routing number not recognized; return to originator'. They say they copied routing from their UI.

Maya (Payments): I pulled the webhook event: payout_id p-8f3a2, provider_response: {"code":"ACH_REJECT","reason":"ROUTING_UNRECOGNIZED","bank_msg":"Routing number not recognized"}. We used routing 021000021 and acct 123456789.

Sofia (Finance): 021000021 is Chase's ACH routing — looks valid. Is the account number short? The customer account ends with 6789, they supplied 123456789?

Maya (Payments): The customer UI showed account as 123456789 but their bank statement shared with support shows account 0123456789 (leading zero). Our system strips leading zeros when formatting numbers for our payments provider. Uh-oh.

Alex (Ops): If we strip leading zeros, many banks will reject because account mismatch. Where's the stripping happening? Probably in our normalization pipeline before provider payload. @payments-bot can you show the normalized payload?

payments-bot: Normalized payout payload for p-8f3a2 -> {"routing":"021000021","account":"123456789","account_type":"checking","name":"QuickPay Inc"} (stored). Original raw_input.account: "0123456789".

Brian (Support): Customer insists they entered 0123456789. They only saw our last 4 as 6789 in UI; they didn't notice missing leading zero. Customer is asking us to reissue.

Sofia (Finance): Two immediate asks: 1) Can we reissue after confirming identity? 2) Any fees on our side for return/re-issue? The bank charged $15 return fee. Please confirm whether to deduct or absorb.

Maya (Payments): Proposed remediation: re-run payout with account padded to original raw_input (0123456789). Also add fix to normalization to preserve leading zeros for account fields. Short-term: manual override for this payout.

Alex (Ops): Quick patch: stop zero-trimming in payments-normalizer v0.9.3; will roll to staging. Can we do a one-off manual reissue while patch is tested? I can ask provider to cancel and create a new ACH with correct account if bank allows.

Brian (Support): Customer ok with reissue if we absorb return fee. They want ETA.

Sofia (Finance): Fine to absorb this one. Please confirm refund flow: provider shows returned funds will be back in 1-2 business days. We'll reissue after funds settle OR we can send wire (faster) if customer prefers and we agree to wire fees.

Maya (Payments): For audit: adding these log snippets to ticket (sensitive parts redacted):
```
EVENT: payout.submit id=p-8f3a2
payload.sent: {"routing":"021000021","account":"123456789","name":"QuickPay Inc"}
provider.response: {"status":"returned","reason_code":"ROUTING_UNRECOGNIZED","bank_note":"Routing number not recognized"}
raw_user_input.account: "0123456789"
```

Brian (Support): FYI customer also attached bank return notice that mentions 'ABA/Routing mismatch with ACH file' and has a contact number.

Alex (Ops): Next steps: 1) Create manual payout with account padded (0123456789) and mark as reissue after funds returned. 2) Deploy normalization patch (hold trimming). 3) Add a validation warning in UI when account starts with 0 — call it out to customers. 4) Add monitoring alert for 'returns where raw_input.account != normalized.account'.

Maya (Payments): I'll do 1 & 3 today. Alex please own deploy of normalization fix, Sofia confirm absorbing $15. Brian update customer that we're reissuing and absorbing fee; ETA 1-2 business days for returned funds then reissue (or offer immediate wire with fee).

Sofia (Finance): Confirmed absorb. Log internal charge to 'customer-fx' and note as one-off.

Brian (Support): Sending update to customer now. Quick mention: can we also check if we inadvertently rewrite leading zeros for IBANs/wires? Might be broader.

Maya (Payments): Good call. I'll scan last 30 days for normalization diffs on account/IBAN fields. If pattern, we escalate to eng-runtime.

Alex (Ops): I'll add a small integration test: submit account "000123456" and assert payload.account == raw_input.

payments-bot: Automated: created support task TASK-5621 -> 'normalize: preserve leading zeros in account numbers' assigned to Alex.

Brian (Support): Thanks team. I'll close ticket once funds return and reissue completes. :thumbsup:

Maya (Payments): Thanks — filing postmortem notes and linking to TASK-5621.
